key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr combined the lowest reported wear rate with the best corrosion resistance among four thermal-spray coatings on 304 stainless steel.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising coating route for stainless-steel components exposed to combined wear and corrosion, while HVOF also delivered strong wear performance.
method: Deposit WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF and HVAF.
Compare microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, volumetric wear rate and corrosion behavior.
Examine wear tracks to identify abrasive and fatigue wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF achieved a wear rate of (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for uncoated steel, and the lowest coating corrosion current density at (1.75±0.02) µA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or the corrosion medium, limiting direct transfer of the performance rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
